picks.title: GitHub open-sources Replica, an AI prototyping tool built by GitHub Design
picks.excerpt: GitHub is open-sourcing Replica, an AI-powered prototyping tool from GitHub Design that turns product ideas into interactive prototypes built with your own design system.
picks.rationale: This is a primary-source release from GitHub's own design team. Replica is an open-source AI prototyping tool that builds interactive prototypes with your own design system, so product designers can try it immediately. The only history match is the 10-10 AWS physical-AI toolchain, which shares the words 'open-sources' but is a different story.

picks.title: Qt Group launches Clate, an AI-native design tool for embedded interfaces
picks.excerpt: Qt Group unveiled Clate, an AI-powered design environment for embedded UIs that combines no-code building, natural-language prompts and production-ready QML output.
picks.rationale: This is a new product launch. Clate takes designers from natural-language prompts to production-ready QML for embedded and device UIs, which narrows the design-to-engineering handoff in HMI work. Nothing on Qt or Clate appears in the 30-day history or in the gadgets published list.

picks.title: Foundry releases Nuke 18.0 in open beta with a Griptape node for AI image and video workflows
picks.excerpt: Nuke 18.0's new Griptape node connects the compositor to Foundry's AI orchestration platform, letting artists run generative image and video workflows - such as generating a dust element - inside the node graph.
picks.rationale: This is a new version release. Nuke 18.0 adds a Griptape node, so compositors can run generative image and video steps inside the node graph, and the open beta is available now. The movies section ran the Griptape Enterprise launch (AWN) on 07-17, which was a different event; Nuke 18 itself has not been published in any section.

picks.title: Vectorworks 2027 AI Visualizer adds Google's Nano Banana 2 and Nano Banana Pro
picks.excerpt: Vectorworks 2027's AI Visualizer palette now offers Nano Banana 2 for fast concept iteration and Nano Banana Pro for presentation images, at 2K with 4K upscaling and up to 14 reference images per prompt.
picks.rationale: This is a new feature inside a professional CAD/BIM tool. Architects and landscape designers get two Nano Banana models in Vectorworks for concept and presentation renders, with 4K upscaling and up to 14 reference images. The history match is the 09-29 Google Flow build pointing to Nano Banana 2.1, which is a different product and a different event.

picks.title: The time AI saves designers usually disappears. Here's how to keep it.
picks.excerpt: What a survey of 521 UX professionals found about where AI time savings go - and how designers can keep them.
picks.rationale: This piece rests on new data, a survey of 521 UX professionals on where AI time savings actually go, and gives designers practical steps to keep that time. That makes it more useful than the opinion essays in the pool. The nearest earlier items are UXC essays on 10-15 ('hourglass') and 10-06 ('skill atrophy'), which are different arguments without this survey.

dedup.note: Dropped as cross-section or published duplicates: Runway App Studio (movies), The Verge Genie 4 (games), Apple Creator Studio (music/gadgets), and both NVIDIA RTX Spark posts (they continue the 10-14 RTX Spark story, and RTX Spark coverage belongs to games/gadgets). Not picked: the Figma generative-plugin version history (close to the 10-28 Figma shaders video, and would have been a second figma pick), the Figma 'agent-ready design system' video (same topic as the 10-24 Figma blog post and the 10-27 UXC MCP design-system post), the Config India keynote (promo), the GitHub Copilot image generation post (would be a second GitHub card, and the dev-tool feature is less design-specific), the Gemini 4 Argon showcase (model promo, and likely to clash across sections), the Lovable ad controversy (a marketing angle), MAI-Image-2.6 GA (an off-list outlet, and a model-availability item), Allplan Max (a second cad pick; Vectorworks has the more concrete feature detail), the Frame.io YouTube short, the Fast Company smart-TV and design-principles pieces (one has no og_image; the other is less design-tool-relevant), and the remaining UXC essays (opinion only; the one UXC slot went to the survey piece). Cross-section check: I exact-checked published_urls.json movies (cgchannel and Foundry entries) and gadgets (no electropages).
